race.name: GFNY José Ignacio
race.tagline: Atlantic wind, open Uruguayan rollers, and 130 kilometers from Pueblo Garzón to the ocean and back.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: Early January is peak summer on Uruguay's Atlantic coast. Riders should expect warm conditions, strong sun, and exposed coastal wind, with little shelter on the long Route 10 section.

terrain.surface: Paved highways and rural roads from Pueblo Garzón to Route 10 and the Atlantic coast.
features: A shared rolling opening from Pueblo Garzón
A long descent toward Las Garzas and the Atlantic
Thirty-four exposed kilometers beside the ocean on Route 10
A rolling final 30 kilometers back toward Pueblo Garzón

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: A scenic, legitimate inaugural GFNY race with a full-distance competitive course. Moderate elevation and first-edition uncertainty keep it below flagship status.

key_climbs: A shared rolling opening from Pueblo Garzón
A long descent toward Las Garzas and the Atlantic
Thirty-four exposed kilometers beside the ocean on Route 10
A rolling final 30 kilometers back toward Pueblo Garzón
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The 34-kilometer Atlantic section, where group position and wind direction can matter more than any single climb.

course_description.character: The competitive route leaves quiet Pueblo Garzón on open rolling roads, descends to the Atlantic, spends 34 kilometers exposed beside the ocean, and returns over terrain that keeps asking for controlled changes of pace. The total climbing is moderate; wind, heat, and the accumulation of rollers are the real selectors.
course_description.signature_challenge: The 34-kilometer Atlantic section, where group position and wind direction can matter more than any single climb.

logistics.airport: Carrasco International Airport (MVD) is the main international gateway; Punta del Este Airport (PDP) is closer when seasonal service fits.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in José Ignacio, Pueblo Garzón, or Punta del Este. Peak-summer demand is high, so book early and confirm race-morning transport.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Pueblo Garzón and the Maldonado coast are known for parrillas, olive oil, wine, and seafood; carry familiar pre-race food because the start village is small.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced the inaugural José Ignacio race in June 2026 for January 3, 2027, adding a peak-summer competitive event between its established Uruguayan editions.
notable_moments: 2026: GFNY announces the new Uruguay race
history.reputation: An unproven but unusually well-defined inaugural race with a clear coastal identity.

biased_opinion.summary: The competitive route leaves quiet Pueblo Garzón on open rolling roads, descends to the Atlantic, spends 34 kilometers exposed beside the ocean, and returns over terrain that keeps asking for controlled changes of pace. The total climbing is moderate; wind, heat, and the accumulation of rollers are the real selectors.
weaknesses: Summer heat can dominate the day
Wind may make the course tactically volatile
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A strong rolling-road target for riders who want a real race without an alpine climbing bill.

final_verdict.one_liner: Atlantic wind, open Uruguayan rollers, and 130 kilometers from Pueblo Garzón to the ocean and back.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A strong rolling-road target for riders who want a real race without an alpine climbing bill.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Punta del Este for more climbing, or GFNY Colonia for a flatter Uruguayan race.
